title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has released its official reply to the 2020 Committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, explaining how it plans to shape policy and oversight around AI use in public services. It highlights commitments to transparency, accountability, and collaboration with stakeholders to ensure AI technologies are safe, reliable, and aligned with societal values.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual explains how it will oversee and manage the use of artificial intelligence in exams and qualifications, aiming to keep tests fair, secure and reliable. The policy was issued after a request from the Secretary of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business, showing government interest in regulating AI in the education sector.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report looks at how copyrighted content is used when building artificial intelligence systems and examines the potential consequences. It evaluates the legal, economic, and societal effects of relying on these works for training, ensuring that developers and users understand the implications of copyright in AI development.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government outlines its commitment to tackling the challenges raised by the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence, stressing the need for robust regulation and investment in AI research. It emphasizes that the nation will take proactive steps to ensure AI development is safe, ethical, and benefits society while maintaining a competitive edge.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document sets out the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of a committee that will review how artificial intelligence interacts with public standards. It also includes frequently asked questions to clarify key issues and guide the committee’s work.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of artificial intelligence. The submission outlines the organisation’s views and recommendations on how AI should be regulated and managed.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explores how artificial intelligence will change the rules that medical products must meet, emphasizing safety, efficacy, and ethical use. It explains how the principles from the AI White Paper can be applied to update regulatory frameworks so that AI-powered medical products are developed and monitored responsibly.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make our organisation the leading AI‑enabled defence force among similarly sized nations. It focuses on building effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI systems to strengthen national security.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport AI Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to take advantage of artificial intelligence benefits. It also outlines steps to control risks and ensure the technology is used safely and responsibly.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report examines how copyrighted material is used in AI system development under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It outlines progress, challenges, and recommendations to ensure compliance and promote responsible data use.
